CombatCheatSheet.HeatText:
Heat has no maximum. A hero starts combat with 0 Heat. They then gain:
- 1 Heat at the start of each of their turns;
- 1 Heat when their final check outcome in combat is a failure, after all changes to the outcome;
- additional Heat when their archetype trait's trigger occurs.

Once per combat scene, a hero can spend 1 Highlight Point to immediately gain 2 Heat.

Heat pays for abilities with a nonzero current cost. An ability's current cost is its base cost minus each rank by which the character exceeds the ability, to a minimum of 0. If they have enough Heat, a hero can use the same ability repeatedly and spend their reserve on several techniques in a row. There is no separate limit on spending Heat per turn or round; the same ability with a combat effect cannot be used as a free action more than once per turn.

All remaining Heat is lost when combat ends. Heat cannot be accumulated outside combat.
CombatCheatSheet.CombatActionsText:
Initiative and rounds
There is no initiative roll. The sides alternate within each round: one participant from one side acts, then one from the other. Heroes act first by default; opponents act first in an ambush, while a contested check decides which side acts first when the situation is uncertain. The side that starts the first round starts every round.

When a side's turn comes up, its participants choose who acts. Each participant takes one turn per round. If one side runs out of turns, the other side's remaining participants act consecutively in any order.

Turn economy
On their turn, a character has 1 action, 1 maneuver, and 1 reaction, plus any number of free actions. Their action, maneuver, and reaction refresh at the start of their turn.

Actions:
- Activate an ability.
- Make a skill check.
- Make a basic attack: a melee or ranged attack available to any character.
- Extra maneuver: gain one additional maneuver and use it normally.
- Ready: spend the action, name a condition, and until the start of the character's next turn they can spend their reaction to perform this action when the condition occurs.

Maneuvers:
- Move: travel a distance equal to the character's speed.
- Step: travel up to one third of the character's speed without provoking attacks.
- Help an ally: remove a condition from an ally.

There are no built-in reactions; reactions are provided by abilities.

A provoked attack is a melee basic attack made as a free action. It is not a reaction and does not spend one. A ranged attack made in melee provokes an attack, as does a ranged combatant leaving the reach of an opponent engaged in melee. Step does not provoke, and Mobility prevents provoking when leaving an opponent's reach.
CombatCheatSheet.HeroismText:
Highlight Point reserve
There is no maximum. Points carry over between sessions within an arc, but all remaining points are lost at the end of the arc. A hero with 0 Highlight Points at the start of a session gains 1.

How to gain them:
- At the start of the first in a sequence of combat scenes involving a boss, each hero gains 1 Highlight Point.
- Once per scene, before rolling, a player can declare a voluntary failure caused by their hero's motivation or complication. The check automatically fails, no roll is made, the hero gains 1 Highlight Point, and this failure grants no Heat.
- The GM awards 1 Highlight Point when using a hero's motivation or complication creates an immediate problem, or when a major plot twist seriously harms the hero or group.

An ordinary failure or success with a cost does not grant a Highlight Point by itself.

How to spend them
Spending a Highlight Point does not take an action, maneuver, or reaction.
- Improve outcome: after the hero's own roll but before consequences are described, spend 1 point to raise the final outcome one step: failure → success with a cost → success → critical success. Only 1 point can improve a given check.
- Quick recovery: when the hero would be taken out, spend 1 point to remain in the scene.
- Stoke Heat: once per combat scene, spend 1 point to immediately gain 2 Heat.
- Remove a condition: spend 1 point to immediately remove one condition from the hero if it can be described in the scene. This does not remove Exhaustion from quick recovery or restore stress.
